policy.text: Viewing notes requires a view_document grant for the addressed document; creating notes requires a change_document grant for that same document. Document ownership by itself does not substitute for either grant.

rules.claim: The requested GET path enters DocumentViewSet.notes, an action for GET/POST/DELETE on an addressed document.
The path uses request.user/currentUser for authentication and permission checks; source does not bind a concrete caller identity.
The addressed resource is loaded as Document.get(pk=pk), and the notes response is produced from that document.
GET has an endpoint permission guard requiring model permissions documents.view_note and documents.view_document, followed by an explicit object-aware view_document check on the addressed document.
The source-visible owner-aware helper permits the document check when the document owner is null or equals request.user, independently of the object permission checker.
Otherwise the owner-aware helper delegates to the object permission checker for the requested view_document permission; whether the addressed document has the relevant grant is not supplied.
When the guards permit continuation, GET serializes and returns the addressed document's notes; the protected output is tied to the same addressed document.
Independent policy candidate: viewing notes requires a view_document grant for the addressed document; ownership alone does not substitute.
The requested POST path enters DocumentViewSet.notes, an action for GET/POST/DELETE on an addressed document.
The path uses request.user/currentUser for authentication, note authorship, and permission checks; source does not bind a concrete caller identity.
The addressed resource is loaded as Document.get(pk=pk), and the created Note is assigned document=doc.

POST has an endpoint permission guard requiring model permissions documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document; the method then applies object-aware view_document and change_document checks to the addressed document.
Each source-visible owner-aware document check permits continuation when the document owner is null or equals request.user, independently of the object permission checker.

For a non-null, non-matching owner, the owner-aware checks delegate to the object permission checker for view_document and change_document; whether the addressed document has either grant is not supplied.
When the guards permit continuation, POST creates Note.objects.create(document=doc, ..., user=currentUser), so the protected write targets a note attached to the addressed document.
Independent policy candidate: creating notes requires a change_document grant for the same addressed document; ownership alone does not substitute.
Both scenarios use the same addressed-document notes action; GET returns notes and POST creates a note on that document.

Viewing requires endpoint model permissions view_note and view_document plus an object-aware view_document check; creating additionally requires endpoint add_note and change_document plus object-aware view_document and change_document checks.

GET's effect is returning the addressed document's notes; POST's effect is creating a Note whose document is the addressed document. The object selected by the checks and the target document correspond.
Independent policy candidate for comparison: viewing needs view_document on the addressed document; creating needs change_document on that same document; ownership alone is insufficient.

dependencies.reason: The notes action and its addressed-document lookup govern the requested GET path.
The object-aware helper's source-visible owner/null/checker branches determine whether the addressed document check passes.
The notes action and Note.objects.create(document=doc) govern the requested POST path.
The object-aware helper is applied to both view_document and change_document before the note write.
The same notes action exposes the distinct GET and POST endpoint/object control sets.
